Lesson 2 of 10 in *Vital, step by step*: everything you need to feel at home in the real Vital plug-in. Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Learn what a wavetable and a wave frame are.
2. Move the wave frame and hear the tone change.
3. Stack two and three oscillators, in tune and a little out of tune.
4. Hear unison.
5. Find the same controls, and more, in the real Vital.
:::

## Oscillators

- An **oscillator** makes the raw sound: a wave that repeats very fast. How fast it repeats is the *pitch*; the wave's *shape* is the *tone* (bright, soft, hollow ...).
- Vital has three: **OSC 1**, **OSC 2**, **OSC 3** (Vital source, oscillator_section.cpp; synth_constants.h). Each has an on switch at its top left.

## Wavetables and the wave frame

- A *wavetable* is a row of single waves, one after another, called *frames*. Vital's tables have 257 frames, numbered 0 to 256 (Vital source, synth_constants.h).
- **Wave frame** picks which frame plays. Turn it and the wave morphs from one shape to the next (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp).
- On this page each oscillator has one table: sine at frame 0, triangle near 85, square near 171, saw at 256. It is modelled on Vital's *Basic Shapes* table; that name and the frame order are this site's guess (unverified).
- A *sine* is the softest wave, a single pure tone. A *saw* is the brightest and buzziest. *Triangle* and *square* sit between them; the square sounds hollow.

## Pitch and level

- **Transpose** moves the oscillator in semitones (a semitone = one piano key), -48 to +48; 12 is one octave (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp).
- **Tune** moves it in *cents*, hundredths of a semitone. Two oscillators a few cents apart *beat*: you hear a slow wobble, which makes the sound thick.
- **Level** is how loud each oscillator is. A new oscillator starts at about 71 % (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp).

## Unison

- **Unison** plays several copies of the oscillator at once, each slightly out of tune, for a big, wide sound. Vital allows 1 to 16 voices per oscillator (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp).
- On this page one **Unison** knob is shared by all three oscillators, up to 8, and while it is above 1 the panel plays one note at a time (this page's engine). The real Vital keeps playing chords with unison on (unverified).

## Step by step

Each step loads a starting patch made on this page (not one of Vital's presets) and plays it. Listen for the one thing it names, then turn the knob it names.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;o1Frame&quot;:0}" data-page="voice"><p><b>A sine.</b> Oscillator 1 on <b>Wave frame 0</b>. Listen: a soft, pure tone like a whistle. Now drag <b>FRAME</b> slowly up to 256 while a note plays.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;o1Frame&quot;:171}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Triangle and square.</b> Frame 171: the square, hollow like a clarinet. Turn <b>FRAME</b> to 85 for the triangle (softer) and then to 256 for the saw (brightest).</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;o2On&quot;:true,&quot;o2Frame&quot;:0,&quot;o2Tr&quot;:12,&quot;o2Lvl&quot;:50}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Two oscillators, an octave apart.</b> OSC 2 is on: a sine, <b>TRANSPOSE</b> +12, <b>LEVEL</b> 50 %. Listen for a sweet whistle on top of the saw. Switch OSC 2 off and on with its switch to hear what it adds.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;o2On&quot;:true,&quot;o2Frame&quot;:256,&quot;o1Tune&quot;:-10,&quot;o2Tune&quot;:10}" data-page="voice"><p><b>A little out of tune.</b> OSC 1 and OSC 2 are both saws, <b>TUNE</b> -10 and +10 cents. Listen for the slow wobble (beating). Set both TUNE knobs to 0: the wobble stops and the sound gets thinner.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;o2On&quot;:true,&quot;o2Frame&quot;:256,&quot;o2Tune&quot;:7,&quot;o3On&quot;:true,&quot;o3Tr&quot;:-12,&quot;o3Frame&quot;:171,&quot;o3Lvl&quot;:60}" data-page="voice"><p><b>All three.</b> OSC 3 adds a square an octave down (<b>TRANSPOSE</b> -12, frame 171). Listen for the weight underneath. Turn OSC 3's <b>LEVEL</b> down to 0 and up again.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-lead" data-page="voice"><p><b>Unison.</b> A lead with <b>UNISON</b> at 4: four copies of each oscillator, spread in pitch. Listen to the width. Turn UNISON to 1 (thin) and to 8 (huge).</p></div>
```

## In the real Vital

What is different in the plug-in and exactly where to find it. Every line names the file of Vital's source code (github.com/mtytel/vital) it was read from; "(unverified)" means it was not confirmed.

- **The wavetable's name** is at the top of each oscillator's display. Click it to open a wavetable browser; the arrows beside it step through the wavetables (Vital source, oscillator_section.cpp). After *Initialize* the name reads **Init** (Vital source, oscillator_section.cpp); what that starting wave looks like is not in the notes (unverified).
- **The pencil** at the display's bottom-right opens the **wavetable editor**, where you can draw and build your own tables (Vital source, oscillator_section.cpp; wavetable_edit_section.cpp).
- **3D / 2D / SP.** A small button at the display's bottom-left switches the picture between 3D, 2D and SP (the spectrum) (Vital source, oscillator_section.cpp; synth_strings.h).
- **Moving the frame.** Drag up and down on the display, or use the mouse wheel over it, or the vertical WAVE FRAME slider beside it (Vital source, wavetable_3d.cpp).
- **Your own sounds.** Drag one audio file onto the display. Where you drop it chooses how it is turned into a wavetable: top part **WAVETABLE**, middle **VOCODE**, bottom **PITCH SPLICE** (Vital source, wavetable_3d.cpp).
- **Spectral morph** (the left menu under the display) changes the wave's harmonics: Vocode, Formant Scale, Harmonic Stretch, Inharmonic Stretch, Smear, Random Amplitudes, Low Pass, High Pass, Phase Disperse, Shepard Tone, Spectral Time Skew (Vital source, synth_strings.h).
- **Distortion** (the right menu) bends the wave: Sync, Formant, Quantize, Bend, Squeeze, Pulse, and FM or RM from another oscillator or the sample (Vital source, synth_strings.h). Each has an amount knob. This page does neither.
- **PITCH, UNISON, PHASE, LEVEL, PAN.** Transpose and tune are in the PITCH group; hold **Shift** while dragging transpose to move in octaves. UNISON has voices (1-16), detune and detune power (Vital source, oscillator_section.cpp).
- **Stacks.** On the ADVANCED tab each oscillator's **STACK** menu turns unison into chords: Unison, Center Drop 12, Center Drop 24, Octave, 2x Octave, Power Chord, 2x Power Chord, Major Chord, Minor Chord, Harmonics, Odd Harmonics (Vital source, synth_strings.h; oscillator_advanced_section.cpp).
- **Where it goes.** Each oscillator has a DESTINATION: Filter 1, Filter 2, Filter 1+2, Effects or Direct Out. At the start OSC 1 goes to Filter 1, OSC 2 to Filter 2 and OSC 3 to Effects (Vital source, oscillator_section.cpp; synth_parameters.cpp). Lesson 3 explains why that matters.

## Try it in the real Vital

Open Vital in your DAW (see [Meet Vital](intro-vital.qmd) to install it) and do these in order.

- [ ] Initialize the preset. Play a key: only OSC 1 is on.
- [ ] Drag up and down on OSC 1's display. Watch the frame number and listen.
- [ ] Click the wavetable name and load a different wavetable. Step through a few with the arrows.
- [ ] Switch the view button between 3D, 2D and SP.
- [ ] Turn OSC 2 on and set its TRANSPOSE to +12 (hold Shift while dragging).
- [ ] Set UNISON voices to 4 on OSC 1 and listen.
- [ ] Click the pencil, look at the editor, and close it with its X.

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does the Wave frame control pick?</b></p><ul><li>Which wave in the wavetable plays</li><li>The volume</li><li>The filter model</li><li>How many voices play</li></ul><p class="ik-why">A wavetable is a row of frames; Wave Frame picks one (synth_parameters.cpp).</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Two oscillators a few cents apart make…</b></p><ul><li>A slow wobble (beating) and a thicker sound</li><li>An echo</li><li>Silence</li><li>A higher octave</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 4.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How far is Transpose +12?</b></p><ul><li>One octave</li><li>One semitone</li><li>Twelve cents</li><li>Half a step</li></ul><p class="ik-why">12 semitones = an octave.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>In the real Vital, how do you open the wavetable editor?</b></p><ul><li>Click the pencil on the oscillator's display</li><li>Double-click the volume</li><li>Open the MATRIX tab</li><li>Right-click the keyboard</li></ul><p class="ik-why">oscillator_section.cpp: the pencil opens the editor.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Where does OSC 3 go in a fresh Init Preset?</b></p><ul><li>To the Effects, not to a filter</li><li>To Filter 1</li><li>To Filter 2</li><li>Nowhere: it is broken</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Defaults: osc 1 → Filter 1, osc 2 → Filter 2, osc 3 → Effects (synth_parameters.cpp).</p></div>
```
